videos.script: Most of a production prompt never changes. The same long guide goes out with every message, a million times, and you pay to have it read every time. {{guide}} A prompt cache lets the provider skip reading what it has seen before. It does not store answers. It stores the work of reading the start of a prompt. {{cache}} The catch is the word start. A cache matches from the first token, in blocks. One block that differs, and nothing after it can be reused. {{blocks}} So you run the same prompt in two orders. Guide first, and every call after the first reads seven blocks from the cache. The bill falls by forty-three percent. {{static}} Message first, and no two calls share even one block. Everything is written, nothing is read, and the bill is higher than with no cache at all. {{first}} Then you check the thing that must not move. The cache changed what you paid. It did not change a single answer. {{compare}}
